newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia welcomes Hun Sen's bid for fresh polls.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia welcomes Hun Sen's bid for fresh polls.

text.p: Malaysia welcomed Cambodian Second Prime Minister Hun Sen's plan to hold free and fair elections to form a new government, Malaysia's national Bernama news agency reported on Monday.
"We certainly would like to see that happening in Cambodia," Bernama quoted Malaysian Foreign Minister Abdullah Badawi as saying.
"After the election, we will see the emergence or the setting up of the government of the people's choice," Abdullah added.
Hun Sen said in a radio broadcast on Sunday that Cambodia must have a free and fair election.

Foreign ministers of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), including Abdullah, agreed unanimously on Thursday to postpone Cambodia's entry into the seven-member grouping due to the crisis in Phnom Penh.
Cambodian First Prime Minister Norodom Ranariddh has fled to France and fighting between forces loyal to the two men July 5 and 6 killed at least 58 people.
Hun Sen has warned foreign governments to stay out of Cambodia's internal affairs. He said Cambodia could even manage without ASEAN if its admission proved difficult.
Hun Sen has not given a date for a new poll but he and Ranariddh agreed last month that the election should be on May 23.
Abdullah said an earlier date would be welcomed.
Malaysia is currently chairman of ASEAN, which also includes Indonesia, Singapore, Thailand, the Philippines, Brunei and Vietnam.
